Planned merger of streaming giants HBO Max and Paramount+ may ultimately fall through.

After Netflix pulled out of the bidding war for Warner Bros. Discovery, the deal was announced in March of this year. However, a federal judge has now issued a temporary restraining order, blocking the transaction from completing, at least for now...

The planned merger

If completed, Paramount would acquire Warner Bros. Discovery, combining its streaming platforms HBO Max and Paramount+ into a single service.

Temporary restraining order

Viewers have reacted coolly to the plan, concerned that it would reduce competition and lead to price hikes. A coalition of 12 state attorneys general shared those concerns and asked a federal court to impose a temporary restraining order to block the deal. The court has now granted that request, according to NBC News.

The temporary restraining order is effective for 14 days, during which the court will hold hearings. Even if Paramount prevails in the case, the merger is also under review by the European Union and the UK government. The Writers Guild of America has also filed an antitrust lawsuit, arguing that the merger would result in job losses and lower pay.
